current_priority: stabilize the curated Skills lane before turning other candidate lanes into systems
rules: Candidate lanes are planning surfaces, not implemented products.
Do not expose private/core project names, internals, or reshaping state in public lane records.
Do not directly write into private/core projects from public governance repositories.
A lane should graduate only when it has a clear owner, public/private boundary, verification path, and maintenance budget.
Prefer small reusable outputs over idealistic full systems.

lanes.label: Project standards
lanes.purpose: Reusable standards, checklists, and decision rules derived from validated practice.
lanes.admission_rule: Only public-safe, generally reusable standards should be published.
lanes.risk: Can become too abstract or over-prescriptive if not tied to real evidence.

lanes.label: Knowledge graph
lanes.purpose: Public-safe graph projections for resources, concepts, lanes, evidence, and lifecycle state.
lanes.admission_rule: Publish derived topology only; keep private/project-specific graph truth private.
lanes.risk: Can leak relationships or become expensive to maintain if over-modeled.

lanes.label: Benchmark and evaluation
lanes.purpose: Evaluation recipes for resource quality, workflow usefulness, generated artifacts, and adoption decisions.
lanes.admission_rule: Benchmarks must define what they measure and what they do not prove.
lanes.risk: False certainty if scores are treated as truth instead of review aids.

lanes.label: Documentation system
lanes.purpose: Reusable documentation structures, user journeys, diagrams, release notes, and closeout evidence.
lanes.admission_rule: Keep public docs focused on external users and public-safe evidence.
lanes.risk: Can become internal-process-heavy and unreadable if not simplified.

lanes.label: Software architecture playbooks
lanes.purpose: Small, reusable architecture review and evolution playbooks informed by real project work.
lanes.admission_rule: Publish generalized patterns only; do not expose private architecture details.
lanes.risk: May duplicate project-native capabilities or become too idealistic for fast-moving teams.

lanes.label: Domain-specific resource packs
lanes.purpose: Focused public-safe resource bundles for a domain, workflow, or learning path.
lanes.admission_rule: Resource packs should be generated from reviewed public-safe records, not hand-curated link dumps.
lanes.risk: Can decay quickly without lifecycle checks.

lanes.label: Private project absorption queue
lanes.purpose: A generic model for preparing public-safe evidence that private/core projects may choose to review.
lanes.admission_rule: The queue can prepare evidence, but private/core projects decide whether to absorb it.
lanes.risk: Must not expose private project identity, internal stage, or project-specific authority.

lanes.label: Community-curated catalogs
lanes.purpose: Community-maintained catalogs of public-safe resources, templates, workflows, and review notes.
lanes.admission_rule: Community suggestions require moderation, provenance, source policy, and lifecycle state.
lanes.risk: Can become noisy or unsafe without strong intake and rejection rules.
